title: Tag Counts
statement:
A blog stores its posts in a `posts` table: `id` (integer key), `title` (text), and `tags` (a `text[]` array of tag names, each tag at most once per post, possibly empty).

Count how many posts use each tag. Return two columns: `tag` and `post_count`. Order by `post_count` from most to fewest, then by `tag` alphabetically. Tags that no post uses do not appear.

Expected output:

```text
     tag     | post_count
-------------+------------
 sql         |          3
 beginner    |          2
 performance |          2
 postgres    |          2
 web         |          2
 css         |          1
 go          |          1
(7 rows)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE posts (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  title TEXT NOT NULL,
  tags TEXT[] NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO posts (id, title, tags) VALUES
  (1, 'Getting started with Postgres', ARRAY['sql', 'postgres', 'beginner']),
  (2, 'Indexes explained', ARRAY['sql', 'performance']),
  (3, 'Your first Go web server', ARRAY['go', 'beginner', 'web']),
  (4, 'Tuning slow queries', ARRAY['postgres', 'performance', 'sql']),
  (5, 'CSS grid in practice', ARRAY['web', 'css']),
  (6, 'Release notes for May', ARRAY[]::TEXT[]);

tests.output:
tag     | post_count
-------------+------------
 sql         |          3
 beginner    |          2
 performance |          2
 postgres    |          2
 web         |          2
 css         |          1
 go          |          1
(7 rows)

tag     | post_count
-------------+------------
 beginner    |          3

(8 rows)

tests.stdin:
UPDATE posts SET tags = ARRAY['postgres'] WHERE id = 1;
DELETE FROM posts WHERE id = 3;
tests.output:
tag     | post_count
-------------+------------

(5 rows)

tests.stdin:
UPDATE posts SET tags = ARRAY['news', 'sql'] WHERE id = 6;
UPDATE posts SET tags = ARRAY[]::TEXT[] WHERE id = 5;
tests.output:
tag     | post_count
-------------+------------
 sql         |          4
 beginner    |          2
 performance |          2
 postgres    |          2
 go          |          1
 news        |          1
 web         |          1
(7 rows)

hints: `unnest(tags)` turns one array into one row per element.
Put `unnest` in the `FROM` clause next to `posts`, then group by the tag it produces.

sql.starter:
-- TODO: turn each post's tags into rows, then count posts per tag
SELECT tags AS tag, COUNT(*) AS post_count
FROM posts
GROUP BY tags
ORDER BY post_count DESC, tag;
sql.solution:
SELECT tag, COUNT(*) AS post_count
FROM posts
CROSS JOIN unnest(tags) AS tag
GROUP BY tag
ORDER BY post_count DESC, tag;
